models.title: Reading · the train that left 20 seconds early

block.label: READING · SORRY, WE WERE EARLY!
block.html:
In Brazil, people often complain because the bus is late. In Japan, people sometimes get an apology because the train is early!

In November 2017, a Tsukuba Express train near Tokyo left Minami-Nagareyama station at 9:44:20. The timetable said 9:44:40. So the train didn't wait the last 20 seconds. The staff didn't check the time carefully, and the doors closed too early. Nobody complained, but the company wrote an official apology on its website: "We deeply apologize for the severe inconvenience."

Six months later, in May 2018, it happened again. A train left Notogawa station, in Shiga, at 7:11:35, 25 seconds before 7:12. The conductor thought the time was 7:11, so he closed the doors. A few commuters missed the train, and the company said the mistake was "truly inexcusable".

People around the world read the news and laughed. In many cities, a delay of 20 minutes is normal. But in Japan, 20 seconds became international news.

blocks.label: READING · NO PLASTIC, PLEASE!
blocks.html:
Marta lives in Porto Alegre and she has a small shop called Bem Pesado. It is a zero-waste shop: there aren't any plastic bags, and there isn't any packaging. Customers bring their own jars, bags and bottles from home, and they buy exactly (ecz-ec-tli) the quantity they need.

"In a normal supermarket, you buy a big bag of rice or a packet of pasta, and you often buy too much," Marta says. "Here, you can buy only a little: 200 (two hundred) grams of rice, a few spoonfuls of coffee, or half a dozen eggs."

The shop sells a lot of things: rice, beans, nuts, olive oil, honey, soap and even toothpaste. There aren't many products, but they are all local. "People think it is expensive," she says, "but when you buy only what you need, you don't throw away much food, so you save money."

Not everything is easy. "Some customers forget their jars," Marta laughs. "And on Saturdays there are too many people and there isn't enough space. But I am very happy. Every month, there are more customers and less plastic."
